note: `gen-class` / `gen-interface` are the COMPILE-TIME supertype spellings and were unread, so the lane's `extends` verdict rested on the belief that `proxy` was the only one. Parse-tree probe: 3 `:extends` sites and 2 `:implements` sites in clojure's own genclass tests, 0 in clj-kondo and core.async. The edge is anchored on `activeFunction ?? currentNamespace` — the CLJ-D48 rule the reify and proxy branches already use — because gen-class is a top-level directive with no enclosing function. The GENERATED class is deliberately NOT minted as a symbol: `:name a.b.Gen` is a class the AOT compiler emits, not a var this file defines, so its name rides in metadata (`genClassName`) instead. Every option shape is pinned, including the two orders (`:name` before and after `:extends`) and the missing `:name`, because a single-pass reader leaves `genClassName` off every edge of a form written `:extends` first. The `proxy` case is pinned in the same file to prove the runtime spelling is unchanged: EXTENDS the first supertype, IMPLEMENTS the rest.
